reason: We pay suppliers at 60 to 90 days, not 50% up front, and a credit check on top is a non-starter. We spend about 9k a year on snagging damage from contingency, and 19 per m2 across a block would cost more than the damage it prevents.
objection: Deposit and balance-before-handover terms, plus a price that costs more than the snagging damage it saves. The glazing subcontractor would also have to agree to work around a coating.
instead: Carry on with no protection and pay for cleaning or replacement at snagging from the contingency, or have the glazing subcontractor put basic protection film on.
would_change_my_mind: 60 to 90 day payment terms with no deposit, a price near 5 to 6 per m2, and a reference from another main contractor showing real savings at snagging.
